title: Replace Notion page content with AI and preview it first
h1: review a notion rewrite before replacing its blocks
description: Turn an old Notion checklist into the current version with AI. Preview the removals and additions, then decide whether the backup covers what matters.
keyword: replace notion page content with ai
keywords: claude rewrite notion page with backup
answer: **see the whole rewrite before the old checklist goes.** this action replaces a notion page's child blocks and offers a dry run first. it can also make a backup. some blocks and nested content stay out of that backup, and a staged replacement can fail halfway. use the preview to decide whether a full rewrite is worth it.

review.by: lead agent, after two independent reviewer passes, against Metal docs and the composio catalog

og_line: a rewrite needs more than a backup.
what:
**use replacement when the old body really should go.** give the bot the page and new text. a dry run shows what it would remove and add without doing it.

it normally archives the old children, then adds the new ones in batches. an optional backup isn't a complete copy of every page structure. inspect complex pages before trusting this route.
uses: **equipment checks:** replace a flat checklist with the new version you approved.
**event instructions:** update a simple page after the venue agrees to the procedure.
**a rewrite decision:** preview the full replacement and decide if small additions would do.

routine.message: on the last wednesday of each month at 14:35, read the cinderbrook equipment checklist in notion. compare it with the latest file in the approved checklists project folder. if the contents match, stay quiet. otherwise run a dry preview and report the blocks affected here. ask me before you change anything. stop if nested content, toggles or sub-pages make the backup incomplete. after i approve, make a backup and replace only that page. report partial failures and never retry blindly.
routine.when: last wednesday of the month at 14:35
routine.needs: access to the approved checklists project folder; notion read and write for inspecting, previewing and replacing the chosen page
routine.output:
cinderbrook checklist preview
- current body: flat checklist blocks
- proposed body: new opening and closing checks
- backup: required before an approved replacement

dry run only. existing page unchanged.

steps: **limit the access.** allow notion read and write for this replacement job.
**read before rewriting.** link the page and have the bot inspect its current contents.
**require a dry run.** read the proposed removals and additions. tell it to wait before making a backup or replacement.
**inspect both copies.** after an approved run, read the new page and backup side by side. pause at any partial failure.
watch: **a half-finished rewrite needs inspection.** old text can go before all the new text arrives. stop, look at what remains and avoid a blind retry.
**keeping old children adds alongside them.** turn off archiving only when that is the result you want.

faq.q: can i see what would change without rewriting the page?
faq.a: **yes. ask for a dry run.** it previews removals and additions while leaving the page alone.

faq.q: does a backup guarantee a full restore?
faq.a: **a backup covers only the content this action can copy.** unsupported blocks and nested content need another plan. leave a complex page alone if losing those parts would break it.

steps: give the replacement text from a file
read the proposed removals and what the backup leaves out

mistakes.mistake: treating backup as a full restore
mistakes.fix: inspect nested content and unsupported blocks first.
open the page and identify what remains before another write.

tip.text: a dry run costs a moment. rebuilding a lost page costs more.

items: the preview shows the intended removals and additions
nested content will not disappear unnoticed
partial failure means stop and inspect
